<B>Depot boxes<N>
<br=5>Whenever you enter the field in front of a depot box, the contents of your personal depot are loaded into it. As a free player, you can store up to 1,000 objects in your box, regardless of their size and weight. Note that if you have a Premium Account, the amount of items you may store in depot boxes is 2000. Once you move away from the box, all contents are saved automatically, and no other player can get access to your depot.

<b>Congratulations!
<br=7><n>You have reached level 20!
<br=5>If you are a premium player and if your character has the necessary funds, you can now promote your character to the elite rank of his vocation!
<br=7>We would like to take the opportunity to remind you that you should keep your account secure. Remember there might be people who try to steal it!
<br=7>Please take a minute and read the following security hints carefully. For further information please see our website.

<b>Welcome to Tibia!
<br=7><n>Greetings wanderer! You are about to enter the mysterious world of Tibia. Fight fearsome monsters, find untold treasures and make your character a true hero of the land! There are many different ways to play Tibia, but keep in mind that there are many others players out there who want to enjoy the game just like you, so please play fair and follow the Tibia Rules at all times.
<br=7>To move your character use the cursor keys or click on a spot on the game window or in the automap. Right-clicking on items, monsters, characters or simply on the map will open context menus in which you can select appropriate actions such as attacking or using things. Items can be moved around by using drag&drop.
<br=7>If you need assistance, click on the 'Help' button to the right. There are several help options to choose from. For instance, the 'Client Help' will provide you with information on important objects on the map or parts of the client program. Also, a flashing exclamation mark will appear in the top right corner from time to time to inform you that further hints like this one you are reading right now are available. To review previous hints click on 'Help', then 'Hints'. For detailed information please read the manual and the 'FAQ' on our offical website www.tibia.com.

limitations: The session serves operations only after Ghidra reports default auto-analysis complete; incomplete analysis does not expose partial results.
The imported Program and temporary project are ephemeral and deleted on close. Annotation operations edit session database metadata; original executable bytes are never written.
Cancelling an active Ghidra request terminates its ephemeral database and discards session annotations. The selected target remains open; the next provider query imports the original artifact again.
Default-space addresses use lowercase 0x-prefixed hexadecimal; other address spaces use <percent-encoded-space>:0x<hex>.

Only Ghidra-defined string Data is observed; packed or undefined string bytes may be absent. Completeness applies to that inventory, and an empty search does not establish that text is absent from the artifact. If an address is known, use read_bytes and xrefs to inspect bytes and references.

Regex mode uses Java Pattern semantics. Matcher or compiler stack exhaustion returns a resource constraint without closing the session; literal mode avoids regex recursion and returns complete matching values.

Windows Ghidra P0 accepts native x86, x86-64, ARMNT (Thumb-2) and ARM64 PE applications and DLLs, and explicitly selected raw 6502 images; managed, hostile, sensitive, and mutable-path targets are unsupported.
The Windows bridge uses authenticated IPv4 loopback because Node path-based IPC does not expose Java AF_UNIX sockets; the endpoint file contains no bearer token.

Windows sessions require the matching packaged Windows x64 native addon, local NTFS targets and runtimes, and Windows 10 or later. Native handles enforce path admission, private DACLs, and Job Object ownership automatically.
